To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATP synthesis from ADP and Pi is catalyzed in the liver by enzymes of the hexose monophosphate pathway and not by mitochondrial ATPase.
1) ATP hydrolysis is not measurable by saturation transfer in the perfused rat liver, and 2) ATP synthesis catalyzed by glycolytic enzymes is measurable by the technique in the absence of glycolysis.

1) the rate of Pi----ATP conversion catalyzed by the mitochondrial ATPase is too low to be detected by NMR; 2) Pi----ATP exchange catalyzed by glycolytic enzymes is detectable by NMR; and 3) Pi----ATPi exchange in the direction of Pi synthesis is not detectable by NNR in the perfused rat liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the study of metabolic regulation in vivo using NMR techniques.
the study of the mechanism of ATP synthesis in the liver and the regulation of the ATPase reaction.

the use of 31P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and the saturation-transfer method to measure the rate of ATP-Pi interconversion in the direction of Pi----ATP in the isolated perfused rat heart and liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATPase of the mitochondria is so slow as to be undetectable by the NMR technique used in this study.
the inorganic phosphorus exchange rate in the liver is not a measure of mitochondrial ATPase activity.
there is no detectable rate of ATP synthesis in the perfused rat liver under these conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glycolytic ATPase is the only enzyme which catalyzes the ATP-Pi exchange observed by saturation-transfer techniques.
the glycolytic ATPase activity is not detectable in the isolated perfused rat.
the ATP-Pi exchange rate is 2.2-2.5 times slower than the rate of glycolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ATPase is not the main contributor to the ATP-Pi exchange.
the mitochondrial ATP synthase rate in rat liver is so low that it does not contribute to the NMR detectable ATP-Pi exchange.
the rate of ATP-Pi interconversion in the direction of Pi----ATP is too fast to be measured in the intact rat liver.
